tone_statements.quote: In Musey there are three level tones, high, mid, and low; and six contour tones, as illustrated in Table 1.2. Table 1.2. The tone patterns of Musey. High t{6 ‘evil’, timus ‘hair’ … Mid koy ‘guest’ … Low va ‘thing’, dél ‘throat’ … High-Low say ‘tea’ … High-Mid gun ‘tree’ Mid-High way ‘sibling’ … Mid-Low sum ‘bear’ … Low-High zéw ‘rope’ … Low-Mid ndar ‘neighbor’ … The tone-bearing unit in Musey is the mora. In nominal stems, lexical tones are associated from right to left.

tone_statements.citation: Shryock, Aaron. 1990. Consonant type and consonantal effects on tone in Musey. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 88(S1): S79. [Abstract, 120th Meeting of the Acoustical Society of America, November 1990.]
tone_statements.quote: In Musey, a Chadic language of northern Cameroon, the tonal pattern of a word is partly predictable from the initial consonant of the word. There are two series of obstruents and two h's that contrast word initially. One series is associated with low initial tone, the other with high or midtone; there are, however, minimal pairs which indicate that the initial consonantal contrast in Musey is independent of the tonal contrast.

tone_statements.n_tones: Low vs High or Mid initial tone mentioned; no inventory count stated

sources.note: No statement on Musey word stress anywhere in 124 pp; the only 'stress' mentions concern English (subglottal pressure in emphatically stressed syllables, p. 2; Keating 1984 on English stressed vs unstressed, p. 108-109). Sec. 1.3.3 'Musey Phonology' (p. 4-7): three level tones H/M/L and six contour tones (p. 5), TBU = mora, lexical tones associate right-to-left in nouns, initial-consonant class (High vs Low group) assigns default M or L and triggers low-tone delinking (p. 5-7); verbs carry grammatical tone.
sources.venue: UCLA Working Papers in Phonetics 89 (UCLA Ph.D. dissertation), iv+117 pp

sources.citation: Duncanson, Robert. 1972. Interpreting tone in the Musey language. Work Papers of the Summer Institute of Linguistics, University of North Dakota Session 16, article 3, pp. 78-99. DOI 10.31356/silwp.vol16.03
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent (full scanned a full-text search for stress/accent: no 'stress', 'accent', 'prominence'). Phonology section (p. 79-80): 28 consonants in High/Low/Neutral sets, 5 vowels with length; 'Musey has three level tones and two contours, rising and falling' (p. 80); verb tone reinterpreted as a two-tone system conditioned by initial consonant class.

sources.locator: JASA 88(S1), p. S79, meeting abstract (sentences 1-3 of the abstract)
sources.note: The tonal pattern of a Musey word is partly predictable from its initial consonant: two series of obstruents and two h's contrast word-initially, one series associated with Low initial tone, the other with High or Mid tone; minimal pairs nevertheless show the consonantal contrast is independent of the tonal contrast. Preliminary acoustics found no systematic VOT or breathiness difference between the series; F0 perturbation at consonant release to be examined; discusses implications for consonant-type/tone (depressor) theory.
